guest.bio_context: Maggie Rose moved to Nashville in 2008 as a teenager and has spent 18 years developing her career as an artist. She was nominated for a Grammy Award for her album 'No One Gets Out Alive' and continues to record and tour while balancing motherhood with her music career.

April 13th: date her son was born, coinciding with a full pink moon
Three months: time between Big Loud's release of 'No One Gets Out Alive' and dropping her
10 years or more: duration Maggie Rose has worked with Narvel Blackstock at Starstruck

pending_qa.q: How did becoming a mother change an artist's creative process and perspective on career ambition?
pending_qa.r: Rose started writing her 'Half Moon' album with Lawrence Rothman and Daniel Tashian while in her third trimester, finishing mixing and mastering when her son Graham was about eight months old. She found the experience creatively heightening and emotionally untangling, and motherhood made her loosen her grip on the seriousness of career, realizing that everything wouldn't fall apart and that it actually made her relationship with her art healthier.

pending_qa.q: What circumstances led to a major label dropping an artist and how did that impact her trajectory?
pending_qa.r: Rose was dropped by Big Loud three months after releasing 'No One Gets Out Alive,' learning the news unceremoniously while thinking she was enjoying a record rollout. Two weeks after being dropped, she discovered she was pregnant. She regained her master's back, submitted for the Grammys, and secured her first nomination while eight months pregnant, eventually signing with One Riot, part of Virgin Music Group.

pending_qa.q: How does a songwriter interpret their own work differently after major life events?
pending_qa.r: Rose's title track 'Half Moon' makes more sense to her now than the day she wrote it, two days before her son was born. She wrote it with the knowledge that her son would arrive on April 13th under a full pink moon, using analogies of motherhood and the moon's phases—how it revolves around something bigger, shows up differently each day with only the light given, and waxes and wanes while returning to itself.

pending_qa.q: What business structures and mentor relationships sustain an independent artist through industry setbacks?
pending_qa.r: Rose has worked with manager and producer Narvel Blackstock at Starstruck for over 10 years, having moved there with her husband who also works with Blackstock. Narvel has functioned as her record label on past projects, telling her 'don't worry about that, we're just going to keep making records' when she was dropped or faced label closures, and providing facilities to record and rehearse.
